name: Posit PBC (formerly RStudio, PBC)
subcategory: data-science IDEs and publishing tools (R and Python)
origin_detail: Founded 2009 in Boston as RStudio by J. J. Allaire (creator of ColdFusion); restructured as a Delaware public benefit corporation in Jan 2020 (Certified B Corp, B Lab score 86.1 in 2019); renamed Posit in Jul 2022 to signal a focus beyond R
openness_notes: Open core with an unusually large open share: the RStudio IDE is AGPLv3 and Posit leads 350+ open-source projects (tidyverse, Shiny, Quarto, tidymodels), spending ~35% of engineering on open source (Dec 2024); revenue comes from proprietary professional products (Workbench, Connect, Package Manager, Cloud) bought by 10,000+ customers. Governance remains company-led, but the PBC charter legally commits it to community benefit.

license_history.note: Year of first IDE release not confirmed in fetched pages; licence is current per repository

license_history.license: Unchanged; company became a public benefit corporation
license_history.note: PBC conversion announced Jan 2020, governance rather than licence change

risk_events: Dependence on the R ecosystem; Jul 2022 rename to Posit to broaden into Python
Dec 2023: laid off Yihui Xie, creator of knitr and R Markdown
Jun 2024: launched a new IDE (Positron) alongside RStudio, a costly platform transition
robustness: Highly robust as a steward of scientific open source: 17 years of operation, PBC and B Corp status (score 92.5 at 2023 renewal), joined the Open Source Pledge (Dec 2024), gave >$3.3M to outside-led projects, and its packages are on CRAN under OSI licences. Privately held with only a minority VC stake (General Catalyst), so it is not under exit pressure; financials are undisclosed.
physical_science_relevance: High: RStudio, the tidyverse, Shiny and Quarto are standard tools for statistics, reproducible analysis and publishing in academic science; Public Package Manager serves 74M+ downloads/month (Q2 2026).
openness_effect_assessment: Posit's heavy open-source investment made R's modern ecosystem (tidyverse, Shiny, RStudio) the default in academic data analysis and built the funnel for 10,000+ paying professional customers. Locking in its mission via a PBC charter (2020) reduced the risk of the relicensing or rent-seeking seen at VC-pressured peers; no licence tightening has occurred.
key_takeaway: Posit is the model of a mission-locked open-core company: a founder-led firm that converted to a public benefit corporation, spends about a third of engineering on open source, and sells enterprise deployment tools. It trades fast growth and a big valuation for longevity and community trust, which suits science users.
